findings.title: A large Native borrowed reply consumes the protected short-IO reserve
findings.trigger: Resident typed results occupy most of budget-minus-IOReserve while a Native invocation retains its initial reply reservation. On settlement, its 12MiB reply does not fit resident credit. The fallback preserves the full reply as borrowed without applying the bounded short-result allowance or a total borrowed-byte bound.
findings.impact: A subsequently admitted healthy short Mongo Native cannot reserve its ordinary 48MB negotiated reply workspace. With no converging IO, start returns definitive capacity failure, despite the documented protected-IO progress guarantee. Slow output can therefore cause NATIVE_NOT_STARTED / RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED for a healthy small request.
findings.proof_limit: The allocation-free ledger probe uses internal reservation APIs and no manual account mutation. It establishes a reproducible protection failure. It does not identify the mutex-held branch of the separate real-CLI failure from periodic snapshots.
findings.separate_live_evidence: Root supplied review81-backend-typed7.txt; lines135 and153 record healthy short Native failure during cross_store_typed_native/1024MiB original pressure hold. This reviewer only read that artifact and did not repeat backend load.
findings.required_validation: After correction, this unchanged desired-behavior probe must pass without larger budgets or artificial owner release. Re-run the unchanged seven clean-artifact typed-memory cases, cross-Store slow Typed/Native health under held output, and source/wire cancel/drain/ConnEnd regressions. Preserve the new failed CLI run and all prior failed/diagnostic runs.
